w: Congressman Mr. Dennis Kucimich and Congressman Mr. Sherrod Brown welcomed Swamishri. Mr. Dennis Kucimich presented a proclamation.
At 9.30 a.m., Swamishri departed from Bhuj and arrived at 9.45 a.m. After darshan at the mandir Swamishri blessed the devotees.

At 10.25 a.m., Swamishri arrived in Narayannagar. The BAPS has built 285 houses after the earthquake ( For details ). Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of the newly built Swaminarayan Mandir and then blessed the assembly.

In the evening, Swamishri visited the village of Moti Mau and then went to Shrijinagar (Nani Mau) and performed the murti pratishtha of the newly built Swaminarayan Mandir and blessed the assembly. The BAPS has built 33 houses after the earthquake ( For details ).

Thereafter, Swamishri traveled 34 km to the village of Gadhshisha. More than 3,000 devotees and well-wishers had arrived from 17 surrounding villages for the satsang assembly. Swamishri addressed the assembly and arrived in Bhuj at 8.30 p.m.
At 7.00 p.m. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly.
After his morning puja, a new publication by Swaminarayan Aksharpith, Footprints, was released by Swamishri.
A lunar eclipse was observed from 5.04 pm to 6.03 pm. Swamishri presided over the eclipse assembly where dhun, bhajan and speeches were made by sadhus.

The celebration assembly of the 220th birth anniversary of Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami commenced at 8.00 pm. Viveksagar Swami talked about the ‘Uniqueness of Aksharbrahma’, Tyagvallabh Swami talked about ‘Unparalleled Aksharbrahma’, Kothari Swami praised about the ‘Matchless Austere Spirit of Aksharbrahma’, Dr Swami talked about ‘Aksharbrahma’s Uniqueness in Spreading the Glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’, Mahant Swami elaborated upon the ‘Unique Gunatit Parampara’. Finally, the assembly was capped by Swamishri’s blessings, “Maharaj came on earth with his abode Aksharbrahma. By realising the latter one attains Maharaj. Swami discoursed about the supreme glory of Maharaj. When one engages in listening to discourses one realizes one’s base nature, because without associating with the holy Sadhu one cannot realize one’s base nature.” The fifth and final arti was performed by Swamishri and the assembly concluded at 10.25 pm.
Akshar Mandir, Gondal, was illuminated with lights and decked with decorations for the Diwali festival.

At 6.25 p.m. Swamishri arrived on the main stage in the mandir grounds to participate in the mahapuja ritual and chopda pujan. The rituals concluded at 7.40 p.m. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Akshar Deri is a great, sacred place. All our wishes are fulfilled here. Yogiji Maharaj had blessed that Maharaj would fulfil the wishes of whoever comes here for darshan and seva. May the New Year usher in happiness and peace in the lives of everyone. Life is full of ups and downs. Difficulties arise but they are resolved by having firm refuge in God. For this one must have faith and trust. One has trust in other things, but not in God. When in misery one questions why God allows such misery. But believing God to be the all-doer, one becomes liberated from such thoughts.”

With the blessings of Swamishri senior sadhus performed the foundation-stone laying ceremony of a shikharbaddh mandir at the birthplace of Yogiji Maharaj in Dhari. Swamishri was in Junagadh and blessed the devotees gathered for the function by phone, “Today, the foundation-stone laying ceremony has been performed by Mahant Swami, Kothari Swami, Tyagvallabh Swami, Ishwarcharan Swami and Viveksagar Swami. I have prayed that God makes you all happier in life and grants you moksha for having offered seva for the birthplace of Yogiji Maharaj.” In the evening satsang assembly in Junagadh Viveksagar Swami, Tyagvallabh Swami and Ghanshyamcharan Swami addressed the gathering of 10,000 devotees. Swamishri was honoured with garlands. Then the youths of BAPS Chhatralaya, Junagadh, performed a traditional dance. Thereafter Swami blessed the evening assembly, eulogizing the saintliness of Gunatitanand Swami and Yogiji Maharaj. At 7.30 p.m. Swamishri’s Harikrishna Maharaj was brought in a decorated palanquin into the assembly hall with great honour and festivity. Senior sadhus performed pujan of Harikrishna Maharaj and the devotees honoured him.

Today was Vijaya Dashami. With special devotion, the sadhus had offered an annakut (a large offering of food) to Thakorji in all three shrines of the mandir. Sitting in his wheelchair, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sang the thal (the food offering song) in the shrine of Ghanshyam Maharaj and was doing darshan. While doing darshan, Swamishri said, "Why is there no dal and rice among all these dishes?"
The sadhus said, "For now, the special dishes have been offered. The dal and rice will be brought afterwards."
This subtle observation by Swamishri, so full of supreme devotion, gave everyone an inner insight.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was sitting to offer his meal to Thakorji. Kalyanmurti Swami, sitting in front of him, said, "Please stay two more days, so that you get more rest."
Swamishri immediately said, "I am always at rest, wherever we go."
After a short silence, the sadhus reminded him again, "Have you thought about what we just requested?"
Harinarayan Swami said, "If you stay, you will get rest."
Swamishri said again, "We are always at rest. In the morning we have darshan of Thakorji, the puja is done, and then we meet the devotees."
Having said this, Swamishri expressed his feelings, "All we have to do is what pleases the devotees, pleases the sadhus and pleases Thakorji!"

ds.t: Where is the dal and rice?
w: Today was Vijaya Dashami (Dussehra). The sants had offered an annakut (a large offering of food) to Thakorji in all three shrines of the mandir with special devotion. Sitting in his wheelchair, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was singing the thal (food offering hymn) and doing darshan in Ghanshyam Maharaj's shrine. While doing darshan, Swamishri said, "Why is there no dal and rice among all these dishes?"
The sants said, "For now the dry dishes have been offered, the dal and rice will be brought later."
This subtle observation by Swamishri, who is filled with supreme devotion, made everyone look within.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was sitting to offer food to Thakorji. Kalyanmurti Swami, sitting in front, said, "Please stay two more days, so that you get more rest."
Swamishri immediately said, "I am always at rest, wherever we go."
After a short silence, the sants reminded him again, "Have you thought about what we requested of you just now?"
Harinarayan Swami said, "If you stay, you will get rest."
Swamishri said again, "We are always at rest. In the morning we have Thakorji's darshan, the puja is done, and then we get to meet the devotees."
Having said this, Swamishri expressed his feelings, "All we have to do is what pleases the devotees, pleases the sants and pleases Thakorji, isn't it!"
This morning, when Mahant Swami Maharaj woke from his rest after the mangala arti, Uttamyogidas Swami asked, "Did you fall asleep?"
"No, I was doing dhun so that it rains," Swamishri said.
Hearing this, everyone bowed to Swamishri, "who wanders the world for the good of others..."

Mahant Swami Maharaj was retiring to rest after his shatpadi (walk of a hundred steps), when Anandanandas Swami showed Swamishri the text on the souvenir gift for "National Convention 18" (NC 18), which carried Swamishri's own sentence: "A Gunatit Sadhu can grant moksha."
Swamishri immediately said, "Only a Gunatit Sadhu, that is the point."

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj set out for the assembly, the driver of the car, Rink Parekh, was overcome with emotion and said to Swamishri, "Swami! I had made a resolve that if I got to drive your car, I would be transformed, and you caught hold of my resolve. I got to drive your car. Now I promise that I will be transformed. Thank you."

Swamishri blessed him. Swamishri is a sadhu like the vadvanal (the fire beneath the ocean that turns salt water sweet) spoken of in the Vachanamrut, in whose company many such salty souls become sweet.

Thousands of letters come to Mahant Swami Maharaj from devotees and well-wishers in India and abroad on the occasion of Diwali and the New Year. It had been arranged that a letter from Swamishri would reach all of them in reply. The English translation of the letter prepared for this was read to Swamishri. Swamishri approved all of it, but pointing to its salutation, he said:
"This should be changed." The letter said, "Dear Devotees...!"
Yogvivekdas Swami suggested an alternative: "Then shall we make it 'Bapa's most beloved devotees!'?"
Swamishri said "Yes." But then he said, "Let us write 'Bapa's most beloved Muktos!'"
The sadhus raised a thought: "But among all of them there are outsiders too, aren't there?"
The sadhus wondered whether such a sectarian salutation would seem appropriate to everyone.
Swamishri said with a sense of their glory, "All are muktas (liberated souls)."
